2224.note: Komáromy prints all four letters in Magyar Történelmi Tár 1906 (REAL-J 4115, opened in pass tc05). They are clear Hungarian with seven single secret signs in all, printed as '(titkos jel)': two each in nos. 25, 26 and 27, one in no. 36. There are no cipher runs and no number groups. Lang's own note (2015, p. 68 n. 85) says only one or two words per letter were left unresolved. This is a printed letter series with scattered sign-words, not an unread cipher, so it is closed as partly_read: the seven signs survive only in the MNL OL E 185 originals, which are not online.

2081.note: Two pages of MHS Ms. Sbd-133 are published on the MHS Beehive blog (Dibbell, 15 May 2009, images diary_003.jpg and diary2_003.jpg) and were viewed. Entries are Arabic day numbers followed by short stroke-sign groups in a stenographic script, and the month heads are written in the same signs. The donor's 1845 note calls it a case for 'skill in stenography', and B. L. Oliver (1842) borrowed Davis's 'treatise on shorthand, which is supposed to be the one used'. Closed as not_cipher: an unidentified shorthand diary, unread (Schmeh and Futility Closet 2026 list it as unsolved). Identifying the system is a job for a stenography specialist, not cryptanalysis.

Wilcox diary 1891-93, 1 folder) says only 'a number of entries in the diary are in code form'; no scan, transcription or description of the code was found, and ArchiveGrid is behind a bot check. 1299.note: No verdict. The Ministère des Armées inventory host still refuses connections (curl TLS error, exit 35, 16 Nov 2026). A web-search snippet of the same record gives 'dépêches de Kerlérec, 23/8/1758 - 25/6/1759, dont quelques-unes chiffrées', filed with papers on the Lacouzinière affair and the Rochemore correspondence. The 23 Aug 1758 start date matches one of the despatches Pusch 2008 decoded from ANOM C13A 40 (ministry plaintext between the lines), and despatches went in duplicate, so this is probably another copy of read despatches. That cannot be proved without the cote and folios. Needs the inventory opened in Chrome, then a match against ANOM C13A 40-41.
1299.access_note: Service historique de la Défense (Marine); inventory at bibliotheques-numeriques.defense.gouv.fr, unreachable from this network.

2489.note: The MNL AdatbazisokOnline records, re-read by curl on 16 Nov 2026, are the archive's own descriptions: 'kis részben megfejtetlen titkosírással' (in small part in undeciphered cipher) for E Fasc. 112 fol. 1-4 (to 'Nathanael', i.e. Rákóczi, 27 Dec, year not given), and 'részben megfejtetlen titkosírással' for E Fasc. 113 fol. 39 (Warsaw, 6 Jun 1708), E Fasc. 112 fol. 38-39 (Warsaw, 31st, month not given) and D Fasc. 83 fol. 4 (s.d.). All are French, anonymous and without images. No decipherment is filed or printed. Promote only as the cluster it is: the cipher passages are short, and the same French Warsaw intelligence series of 1708 is already catalogue 2475 (A1 Fasc. 11, open), so the lead agent may prefer to merge these folios into 2475.

1904.note: The MNL records (adatlap 9367-9369, re-read by curl 16 Nov 2026) give each of nos. 7950-7952 as an original 'titkosírással írt levél' from Újvár, July 1710, with no decipherment noted: 7950 Nagyszegi and Ordódy, 10 Jul 1710, 6 p.m.; 7951 an unsigned enclosure of it ('A. 41. Mell.', note 'Triplica (?)'); 7952 Szluha, 10 Jul. The one doubt is no. 8939 (adatlap 10341), a copy of the same writers' letter of 7 Aug 1710 noted 'előző titkos írással írt részeinek feloldását is tartalmazza'. Most naturally that means it carries the decipherment of its own preceding cipher parts, but it could mean those of an earlier letter, possibly no. 7950. Károlyi's chancery register (Extractus Literarum p. 974-975) also summarised these letters. If 8939 or the Extractus gives 7950's content, that letter is read; 7952 (Szluha) is untouched by either doubt.
